terms.comment: Classically a neck-cloth worn by the sick or the soft (Hor. S. 2.3.255; Quint. 11.3.144; Mart. 14.142; Lewis & Short), which the lexicon also gives for a scarf; Traupman uses it for the necktie. Lewis & Short marks the ō long, from faucāle.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 117, 350, 394, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
